coverage.main: Read all sixteen pages of arXiv 2012.03528v1 (NeurIPS 2020): Sections 1-6, Tables 1-4, Figures 1-4 and references, plus the appended Supplementary Material (Sections A-F: frozen-h fine-tuning Figures 5-6, benign accuracy Table 5, ILA re-interpretation, FGSM Tables 6-7, DI2-FGSM/PGD Tables 8-9, other-epsilon Tables 10-13). The NeurIPS proceedings PDF was not retrieved separately.
coverage.supplement: The supplementary material is appended to the arXiv PDF and read.
coverage.excluded_results: White-box source columns (e.g., VGG-19* in Table 2) and the test-loss curves (supplement Figure 6) are excluded.

result_groups.locator: Section 5.1 (pp. 5-6); Section 3.1 Figures 1-2; Tables 1-4; Figure 4; supplement Figure 5, Tables 6-13
result_groups.population: 5,000 test instances per dataset 'that could be classified correctly by all the victim models'; VGG-19 (CIFAR-10) and ResNet-50/Inception v3 (ImageNet) sources; normally trained victims (WRN, ResNeXt, DenseNet, PyramidNet, GDAS; Inception v3, DenseNet, MobileNet v2, SENet, PNASNet)
result_groups.outcome: success (transfer) rate of untargeted L-infinity attacks
result_groups.evidence: The sample is explicitly restricted to instances every victim classifies correctly, and all competitors are evaluated on the same 5,000 instances. No source-success rule is stated.

result_groups.population: Examples from the ResNet-50 source against an ensemble-adversarially-trained Inception and a PGD-trained robust ResNet (MadryLab)
result_groups.outcome: success rate / 'victim error rate' at epsilon 0.1, 0.05, 0.03 (in-text values)
result_groups.evidence: It is not stated whether these robust models were part of the correctness filter; the robust ResNet result is described as an error rate.

f1.evidence: Benign test accuracy is reported for all normally trained source and victim models (CIFAR-10 test set; 50,000 ImageNet validation images), but not for the two robust victims.

f2.evidence: The main scope is explicitly clean-correct for all victims (yes); the robust-victim scope is unresolved. Positive conditioning evidence.

f3.evidence: No source-success rule or explicit inclusion statement in either scope.

f4.evidence: Per-victim two-decimal rates over the stated 5,000 instances have 0.02% resolution and are candidates for unique count reconstruction; they were not extracted cell by cell here. Average columns and the robust-victim scope do not identify counts.

f5.evidence: Untargeted L-infinity attacks with epsilon in {0.1, 0.05, 0.03} (and 16/255, 8/255, 4/255 in supplement F).

f6.evidence: The official repository releases attack and test scripts and links a Drive folder of pretrained models. The README asks users to create selected_cifar10.csv and selected_imagenet.csv themselves, so the exact 5,000-instance samples are not released. Not executed.

artifact_checks.result: Linked in the paper. Listed via the GitHub API (74 files, head 10 February 2023): attack/cifar10/attack_vgg19.py and test.py, attack/imagenet/attack_resnet50.py and test.py, model definitions (including GDAS); README links pretrained models on Drive and instructs users to write their own selection CSVs. Not executed.

bounds_checks.reason: Rates are over instances all victims classify correctly, so no unconditional matched bound applies.
No clean accuracy is given for the robust victims on the evaluated inputs.

limitations: Non-blind evidence audit. Count reconstruction over 5,000 is feasible for per-victim cells but was not performed.
